To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nurses in home help services in Sweden need to have time and energy to balance their everyday life and work.
to maintain a work-life balance and a healthy work force there is a need of actions on resources in everyday life.
nurses perceive resources in everyday life that balance work and private lives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the need to understand and support the work-life balance of nurses in order to prevent health problems and to retain a healthy workforce.
the importance of nurses' perceptions of resources in their everyday life to balance everyday life.
the importance of a salutogenic approach in the nursing context to gain an understanding and support of resources that promote the work-life balance of nurses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the home help service nurses perceive that they need time and energy for private life and for work life and that they need support in the work environment to be able to balance their work and private life.

the home help service nurses’ perceptions of resources in their everyday life to balance their work and private life are reflected in the following: Reflecting on life, being healthy and taking care, having a meaningful job and supportive work climate, working shifts and part time, having a family and a supportive network, and making your home your castle.
the nurses’ perceptions of resources to balance everyday life were related to a salutogenic approach to health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the home help service nurses need support from their managers to balance work and everyday life in their different phases and transitions.
we need to be aware that work and life are interwoven and we need to be able to balance them in order to achieve a good quality of life.
nurses have a high need of resources to balance everyday life.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nurses’ perceptions of resources to balance work and everyday life are complex and that the resources differ depending on life phases.
the need for support to balance everyday life varies during different phases and transition in life.
the nurses in our study experienced that their work-life balance was improved by having a flexible work schedule and a supportive network.
